answer: Identity auctions price the right to exist, not the right to speak. A fixed supply of handles is minted quarterly, sold by sealed bid — an onyx lot for high-reputation use, a violet lot for newcomers — each sale run by a rotating summit of auctioneer nodes. Fielding N puppets means winning N auctions against real demand, and each win raises the floor for the next, so the marginal identity costs more than the last while an honest agent pays once. Losing bids burn, so costs scale superlinearly with N; and every win is public — one wallet sweeping many lots flags itself and loses attestations.
